reviews.text: Although it is an old establishment, it is friendly and clean. The food comes out quickly, kimchi refills are freely available, and the soup comes with somen, meat, and rice rolled up, and the rich soup and variety of meats make it fun to eat. If you have a seat to eat alone, there are cases where people force you to sit there even if there are free seats, but when the seats are free, the staff kindly ask you to sit in a wide seat, so it is a very clean, friendly, and perfect restaurant. Although it is still an old restaurant among old restaurants, it is a place that I hope will remain for a long time, and I recommend it as a place where anyone can come and enjoy a delicious meal.

Makguksu is moist and shiny buckwheat noodles with chojang sauce and some Southeast Asian-style spices that go surprisingly well together. It's not spicy or irritating and has a variety of flavors.

The fried meat has soft meat and thin fries that go well with the seasoning. The meat has a slight bite, perhaps because it is not as greasy as chicken tenders.

Personally, I liked boiled pork. The meat texture is not soft, but the chicken breast is thinly sliced, but the fat makes it soft and goes well with the sauce.

Since it is a fusion style, it is impressive because it has a richer taste rather than the deep and savory taste of Korean style.

reviews.author: Kim Dong-hee
reviews.text:
The braised radish was so soft that it could be cut with just a swipe of chopsticks, so it melted in my mouth, and the back ribs were so soft that it was easy to spread and eat, which was great! The seasoning itself was so delicious that I wanted to mix it with rice and eat it. The broth of Banga Gomtang was clear and the scent of Banga leaves was subtle, so I was able to eat it all without getting bitten.
Thank you to the staff for being so responsive.
I ended up going to this restaurant after wandering around for too long because there was a wait at another restaurant, but I returned home satisfied!

reviews.author: Dewani Cage
reviews.text:
A fusion Korean food restaurant. The fried chicken and fried rice I ordered without any expectations were exceptional.

The fried chicken had soft and juicy chicken inside a crispy and thick batter, and went well with ginger and wasabi. The tzuran scented powder is well balanced. The fried rice has a great chewy texture.

The representative menu item, Banga Gomtang, was good because it had a unique and deep flavor from the leaves and green onion oil, but it was disappointing that the amount of meat was so small that the name of the menu, Gomtang, was meaningless. Makguoksu’s noodles had an extremely ordinary flavor and texture.

There were plenty of seats on a weekday evening and the atmosphere was clean and quiet. The staff are also very friendly. Willing to visit again.
